newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay bourses shut for local holiday.
newsitem.headline: Bombay bourses shut for local holiday.

text.p: Stock markets in Bombay, India's commercial capital, were shut on Tuesday for a local festival and reopen on Wednesday, dealers said.
But New Delhi, Calcutta and Madras exchanges are open for trading.
On Monday, Indian blue chips ended lower in quiet trading as players waited nervously for a confidence vote in the government at the end of the week, traders said.
Both domestic and foreign funds remained on the sidelines, and are likely to stay there unless there is a fresh twist in New Delhi's politics ahead of Friday's vote.
"The uncertainty is increasing rather than decreasing," said Subra Subramanian, director at securities firm H.G. Asia. "This weekend has not helped much."
On Monday, the ruling United Front alliance said it would hold talks with major political parties on April 9 on the budget vote.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index ended 29.88 points or 0.84 pct down at 3,429.26 on Monday while the National Stock Exchange, also based in Bombay, closed 10.10 points down at 990.90.
